Introducion (Part 2)

The data used in this CP is the bloodp data containing blood pressure measurements from a clinical trial. Familiarize youself with the data by loading the data with data(bloodp) and inspecting the data dictionary ?bloodp.

Long and wide format

This data set contains all measurements for each patient in a single row (wide format). To analyze the data, these measurements may have to be put into separate rows (long format). Package reshape2 contains functions to change a data set between long and wide format.

The function melt changes from wide into long format.

    library('lumc.dabs')
    library('reshape2')
    data(bloodp)
## Warning in data(bloodp): data set 'bloodp' not found
    d <- bloodp
    dLong <- melt(bloodp, c('id', 'group', 'SBP_t1', 'age', 'sex'), c('SBP_t2', 'SBP_t3', 'SBP_t4'), variable.name = 'repeat', value.name = 'sbp')
    # order data set by patient id
    dLong <- dLong[order(dLong$id), ]
    head(dLong)
##     id     group   SBP_t1 age    sex repeat      sbp
## 1    1 Treatment 167.6409  74   Male SBP_t2 162.4028
## 133  1 Treatment 167.6409  74   Male SBP_t3 166.5862
## 265  1 Treatment 167.6409  74   Male SBP_t4 157.8374
## 2    2 Treatment 155.8604  83 Female SBP_t2 153.8804
## 134  2 Treatment 155.8604  83 Female SBP_t3 146.7374
## 266  2 Treatment 155.8604  83 Female SBP_t4 147.9793

The first argument is the data set in wide format. The second argument are so-called id.vars, which identify the units (mice) in the data. Values of these variables are repeated for each measurement in the output data dLong. The third argument contains the repeated measurements on the unit (mouse). For each of these columns, a new row is created in the output data per unit. The final arguments determing column names in the output data.

Check dLong and make sure you understand how it relates to the original data d.

A data set in long format can be converted back to wide format using function dcast.

    d1 <- dcast(dLong, id + group + age + sex + SBP_t1 ~ `repeat`)
## Using sbp as value column: use value.var to override.

This function takes two arguments: the data in long format and a formula of the form id.vars1 + idvars2 + ... ~ measruement. The variables on the left hand side are again the identifying variables and the right hand variable is the variable identifying the measurement. The remaining variables are put into separate columns.

Check that d and d1 are identical for the shared columns.

Analysis of the bloodp data

Q1: Naive analysis

The research question is whether treament (group) has an influence on systolic blood pressure (SBP_t*). Conduct a naive analysis where only the first measurement is used as outcome (SBP_t2). Correct you analysis for age and sex by adding them as covriables. What is your finding?

fillin:

Q2: Improved analysis

Blood pressure varies substantially between individuals. This variation might obscure the treatment effect. Which variable is a good predictor (influential variable) of blood pressure after treatment? What are the results of your improved analysis?

fillin:

Q3: Long format data analysis

A second idea is to use all measurements and use the long format data to strengthen results. Use outcome sbp from dLong as outcome, again correct for age and sex and the addtional variable from the previous question. What is your finding? What are your concerns?

fillin:

Q4: Investigate residuals

You can get residuals from your model by using resid <- lm(sbp ~ ..., dLong). Replace your formula in the following code to get the plot:

l1 <- lm(sbp ~ group, dLong)
plot(residuals(l1))

How do you judge the residuals?

fillin:

Q5: Use data summaries (graded)

We switch back to the wide format. A data summary can be directly computed as the outcome of the model: lm((SBP_t2 + SBP_t3 + SBP_t4)/3 ~ group, bloodp). Here, we take the average of the three non-baseline SBP measurements. Add the other covariables from above.

What is your finding about the effect of group? Compare with the other models and give reasons for your findings.

fillin:

Q6: Residuals of data summary model

Use your code from Q4 to produce a residual plot for the data summary model. Interpret.
